desktop.justification: Kept at spec. Evidence is the largest genuinely prepared key count at 1M rows: 3 keys (date, amount, ratio), staged one column at a time because a 3-column batch's staging peak exceeds the 64 MiB D prepared budget while the 3 retained columns fit; zero source column reads. COVERAGE GAP: 4-8 prepared keys at 1M rows are unmeasurable under the D budget; the 8-key run is a fallback diagnostic only. p95 4362.5 ms (4.4x); 2-key 3641.2 ms, 1-key 3101.6 ms. No loosening. Unmet sort thresholds are carried by plan S8.6 (sort performance). Desktop D measurement (Chrome 155 headless, M4 Pro); see docs/validation/interactive-viewer-performance.md.

desktop.justification: Kept at spec. ADMITTED run: the 239 MB resident F4 source is charged to the D worker pool and the sort charges only its own dictionary references (ownership-aware accounting); kernel aggregate peak 416,190,530 B within 512 MiB. The prepared cache cannot hold 1M strings, so keys are read from the resident source. p95 7648.4 ms (1.9x): recorded finding; collation semantics are never relaxed and loosening >2x needs an amendment. Unmet sort thresholds are carried by plan S8.6 (sort performance). Desktop D measurement (Chrome 155 headless, M4 Pro); see docs/validation/interactive-viewer-performance.md.

natural-text-sort-1m.note: Admitted run. Kernel phases (p50): dictionary collation rank 4289 ms, row merge 2078 ms, key read 589 ms.

diagnostics.reason: FALLBACK diagnostic, not threshold evidence: the D prepared budget holds only 2 of these 8 1M-row key columns after staging (the string lanes are larger than the numeric ones that allow 3), so the remaining keys are read from the source inside the measured operation (1536 source column queries per kernel run). It measures a different boundary from spec §12.2.
